transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you in today?

Yeah… I’m here because I can’t really get through a normal day anymore. I spend most of it going back over things in the house, like the outlets, the locks, tools if I’ve used them or even just passed near them, and dust or little bits of dirt that I feel like I need to fix or check again.

It’s not like I check once and then feel done. I’ll look at a lock, touch it, maybe pull on it, walk away, and then this feeling comes back like, “Are you sure?” So I go back. Same with outlets—like I’ll stare at them or make sure nothing’s wrong, and even after I do it, I still don’t feel settled. With tools, I’ll keep making sure they’re put away right or not dangerous somehow. And dust… I know it sounds small, but I’ll notice something and then I’m stuck dealing with it, and then checking around it, and then fixing something else.

It just goes on and on until I’m exhausted. By the end I’m worn out, but I still don’t really feel sure enough to leave things alone. That’s the part that’s been making me feel like I need help, because it’s taking up most of my day.
When you’re going back to check things like the locks or outlets, do you have specific thoughts that come up—like fears that something bad might happen if you don’t check them again?

Yeah, definitely. It’s not just checking for the sake of checking, at least it doesn’t feel that way. I’ll know, on one level, that I already did it right. Like if I was near an outlet or did anything with a tool, I can remember looking at it, putting things away, making sure it was fine. But then this thought just kind of jumps in, really sharp, like, what if there’s a loose wire you missed and the house burns down? Or what if there’s a nail or something small you didn’t notice and my wife steps on it or gets hurt because of me?

And I’ll try to tell myself, “No, you already checked that, it’s fine,” but it doesn’t really work. The thought gets louder, almost like if I don’t go back, then I’m choosing to let something bad happen. I hate it. They’re ugly thoughts, and I don’t want them, but when I try to push them away they come right back stronger. That’s usually what sends me back to look again.
